proof.visibleText: search · search Community Solar Policy in Barbados ## Barbados community-solar policy: current orientation **Status checked: July 31, 2026** Barbados has a functioning framework for distributed and independent renewable generation, but it does **not appear to have a dedicated “community solar” statute or a U.S.-style virtual-net-metering/subscriber-credit programme**. Projects described locally as community solar generally operate as licensed independent power producers selling electricity to Barbados Light & Power Company Limited (BLPC), with community participation achieved through equity ownership rather than allocation of production credits among subscribers. This is an inference from the current legislation, tariff structure and published project model. ([energy.gov.bb](https://energy.gov.bb/publications/electric-light-power-act-supporting-documents/)) ### 1. Government legislation and policy - The principal electricity law is the **Electric Light and Power Act, Cap. 278**, originating as the Electric Light and Power Act 2013 and amended in 2015 and 2019. It establishes licensing for generation, storage, transmission and distribution, dispatch, and electricity sales. The 2019 amendments also require the utility’s Grid Code to be approved by the Fair Trading Commission (FTC) and Chief Electrical Officer. ([energy.gov.bb](https://energy.gov.bb/our-publications/barbados-legislation/)) - Generation intended to supply another person generally requires a generation licence, subject to statutory exemptions. Storage supplying the public grid may also require a storage licence. ([energy.gov.bb](https://energy.gov.bb/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Electric-Light-and-Power-Amendment-Act-2019.pdf)) - The Energy Ministry is still publishing a **draft Electricity Supply Bill 2023.3** for public comment; it should not be treated as enacted law. The approved legislation page continues to list the Electric Light and Power Act and its amendments as the governing renewable-energy legislation. visualContext.summary: search · searchIndependent Perspective on Community Solar in Barbados## Barbados community-solar policy: independent assessment ### Bottom line Barbados **does not appear to have a formal community-solar or virtual-net-metering framework** under which an off-site project allocates generation credits

proof.visibleText: search · search Independent Perspective on Community Solar in Barbados ## Barbados community-solar policy: independent assessment ### Bottom line Barbados **does not appear to have a formal community-solar or virtual-net-metering framework** under which an off-site project allocates generation credits directly among multiple subscribers’ Barbados Light & Power accounts. Barbados instead uses a **generator-sale model**: 1. A licensed renewable-energy system supplies electricity to the grid. 2. Barbados Light & Power purchases the generation under a Feed-in Tariff or legacy Renewable Energy Rider. 3. The generator or project owner receives the payment. 4. Any participating households or investors receive benefits through private ownership, dividends, leases or contractual distributions—not standardized utility-bill credits. BLPC describes its current arrangement as charging customers normally for all consumption while separately crediting or paying for renewable generation. That is **net billing/FIT treatment, not virtual net metering**. ([support.blpc.com.bb](https://support.blpc.com.bb/support/solutions/articles/42000060966?utm_source=openai)) ### What “community solar” currently means in Barbados The term is being used for at least two commercially different structures: - **Community Solar Gardens:** Blue Circle Energy and Sol Ecolution described a portfolio of 33 plants across Barbados, totalling about 23 MW and incorporating the required 30% domestic ownership component. The available description does not identify household subscriptions or allocation of production credits to individual electricity accounts. ([energy.gov.bb](https://www.energy.gov.bb/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Energy-Bulletin-2022-Single-Pages.pdf?utm_source=openai)) - **Remote-panel investment:** Cloud Solar offers participants remotely hosted panels. Generation is pooled and sold to BLPC, with the economic return handled by the company’s platform. This broadens investment access but is not regulated utility-administered virtual net metering.
